evidence.why: Complete factor construction and signed counted multiplication loop.

facts.rationale: Replaces an overly unconditional unchanged claim with exact guard, count and floating-point qualifications.
facts.value: Independently composes non-unit Y-scale, non-null x197C and is_metal factors, then multiplies x2D0->x14[i] for signed indices 0 <= i < x28. Nonpositive counts cause no element writes but do not bypass the initial x2D0 dereference or factor calculation. There is no local capacity check or reset; direct repeated nonidentity applications can compound. With no modifiers, multiplication by 1 is still executed and is an ordinary numeric identity for finite values, not a universal bitwise no-op for exceptional floats. The body performs no action-state or timer writes.

evidence.why: Entire reset, modifier, callback and optional postprocessing sequence.
Active callback table consists of per-kind special-attribute loaders.

facts.rationale: Preserves verified ordering while removing unsupported global idempotence and callback-effect guarantees.
facts.value: Resets co_attrs, x294_itPickup and x2C4 from ft_data, then applies non-unit Y scale, x197C, is_metal and x2229_b1 branches in that order. It asserts a non-null kind-indexed callback and calls it synchronously without a local kind bounds check. After dispatch it conditionally modifies x2D0 and, under x2222_b0 and non-unit Y scale, x2CC fields x14/x18/x1C through ftDonkeyAttributes*. Only the three initial blocks are visibly reset here; whole-pipeline idempotence depends on callback restoration of optional special data. No direct timer or action-state writes occur in this body, but callback effects and preservation of the live GObj/Fighter must be verified separately.

evidence.why: Signature, assertion and all arithmetic branches.

facts.rationale: Qualifies the previous pure-helper wording while retaining the source-level scalar contract.
facts.value: Source signature float(float base_value, float scale, float response_coefficient). Normal arithmetic depends only on these arguments and preserves the semantic unit of base_value; scale and coefficient are dimensionless response controls. The function first asserts scale != 0, including before a zero-coefficient return. It is not unconditionally side-effect-free because assertion diagnostics and floating-point effects are possible. There is no explicit positivity, finiteness or nonzero-result guarantee and no guard against a zero denominator produced by its reciprocal branch.

evidence.why: Override, strict comparison and alternate equality branch.

facts.rationale: Records the important differing equality and optional-override behavior demonstrated by cross-file consumers.
facts.value: Returns the negation of the common x310 parameter transformed by fighter Y scale and the x30 coefficient, with no fighter writes. Ordinary contact consumers use self_vel.y > threshold for the alternate path and otherwise basic landing, so equality takes basic landing. FallSpecial uses a short-circuit override or strict self_vel.y < threshold for LandingFallSpecial; absent the override, equality takes the alternate path. Under ordinary unordered float comparisons, NaN follows those respective else branches. Negation alone does not establish a universally negative returned value.
